title: JUDGE PASSES
full_story:
Courts across Illinois’ Second Judicial Circuit are closed today, in honor of Associate Judge Jerry E. Crisel, who died Friday at age 77 after a brief illness.

The Office of the Chief Judge and the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office announced that today’s court hearings are continued to a later date, and circuit clerks offices will be closed across counties in the circuit, including Jefferson, Wayne, and Edwards.  Other county courthouse offices will remain open.  People with scheduled hearings will be notified of new dates, and defendants are urged to keep their mailing addresses current with their local circuit clerk.

Crisel died at his home in Albion and was appointed an associate judge in 2013 after previously serving as Edwards County State’s Attorney and as a public defender in Edwards, White, and Jefferson counties.

Funeral services for Jerry Crisel are this morning at the Johnson and Vaughn Funeral Home in Fairfield, with burial to follow in Centerville Cemetery.

title: ALMA MAN INJURED
full_story:
An 18-year-old rural Alma man was injured in a rollover crash Saturday night west of I-57.

Marion County Sheriff’s deputies say 18-year-old Hudson Moore lost control while swerving to miss a deer near Kinoka and Hoard Roads at 10:18 pm.  His vehicle overturned and came to a stop.  Moore was already out of the vehicle when emergency crews arrived.

Kinmundy-Alma firefighters and EMTs checked him at the scene, and he turned down hospital treatment.

title: EDS SCHOLARSHIPS
full_story:
Walker Isle and Eric Locke, students in Frontier Community College’s Electrical Distribution Systems (EDS) program, each received the Wayne White Electric Cooperative Scholarship and the Earl Pottorff Memorial Scholarship for the 2026–2027 academic year.  Isle also received the Steve Rafferty Memorial Scholarship for the 2026-2027 academic year.

The EDS program prepares students to build, repair and maintain the electrical distribution systems that deliver power to homes and businesses.  Students study electrical theory and gain hands-on experience climbing utility poles and practicing techniques for rescuing an injured worker from a pole.

Students also earn two credentials that can expand their job opportunities.  Flagger certification qualifies them to direct traffic at work sites, a skill they can use on utility and construction projects.  Students also earn a statewide spray applicator license for jobs that require the use of restricted-use pesticides.

For more information about the EDS program, call Frontier Community College at 618-842-3711 or visit iecc.edu/fcc/eds.

title: SCOUTING FOR FOOD RESULTS
full_story:
Greater St. Louis Area scouts collected over 125,000 food items in southern Illinois and southeast Missouri for local food pantries on November 21st.  Scouts collected items as part of their Scouting for Food drive.

They said the amount of food collected could feed over 13,000 people in the region for a day.  Across the 63 counties they cover in Illinois and Missouri a total of 1,682,011 food items were collected.

title: CLICK IT OR TICKET
full_story:
As families and friends gather to celebrate Thanksgiving, the Illinois Department of Transportation, Illinois State Police and law enforcement agencies throughout the state are ramping up enforcement efforts and reminding the public to buckle up and drive sober.  Hundreds of seat belt enforcement zones and other patrols will be looking for seat belt law violators and impaired drivers through the Thanksgiving weekend.

“Thanksgiving is a time to celebrate with loved ones, but increased holiday traffic also brings a greater risk of crashes,” said Stephane B. Seck-Birhame, bureau chief of Safety Programs and Engineering at IDOT.  “Whether you’re traveling across town or across the state, always buckle up, make sure children are properly secured in an appropriate car seat and never get behind the wheel impaired.  A few simple decisions can make all the difference in getting everyone home safely.”

During the Thanksgiving holiday period last year, IDOT reported nine fatal crashes, resulting in nine fatalities in Illinois.

“The holidays are a time to enjoy family and friends, but only if you arrive alive at your destination,” said ISP Division of Patrol Col. Chris Owen.  “If you are traveling for the holidays, make sure to wear your seat belt and don’t drive while impaired.  ISP troopers see every day how those two simple steps save lives.”

The national “Click It or Ticket” and “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” campaigns combine public education with increased law enforcement efforts to reduce crashes, injuries and fatalities.

As you make your Thanksgiving plans, keep these important safety tips in mind, buckle up every trip, every time, plan ahead for a sober ride, use a safe transportation option, never drive impaired, and speak up to prevent impaired driving.

The increased traffic enforcement is made possible through federal funds administered by IDOT and supported by ISP and local law enforcement.  The effort coincides with IDOT’s “It’s Not a Game” radio, digital and TV campaign, which reminds the public of the consequences of impaired driving as well as distracted driving, work zone safety, pedestrian safety, motorcycle awareness and occupant safety.
